headline: US government launched mass spying campaign against leftwing and anti-ICE protesters
summary: Newly disclosed records reveal the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) used undercover agents, infiltrated Signal chats, and obtained financial records of unions and non-profits opposing Trump's immigration crackdown. The operation, dubbed "Operation Puppet
details: Newly disclosed records reveal the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) launched "Operation Puppet Master" to extensively spy on leftwing organizations and anti-ICE protesters in Minnesota and New York. This vast operation aimed to identify a "network of conspirators" organizing against US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

DHS agents infiltrated community meetings in the Twin Cities and New York City, joined Signal chats, and obtained financial records. This surveillance targeted mainstream unions and left-leaning non-profit groups opposing the Trump administration's immigration policies.

The records were released as part of a criminal case filed by the Department of Justice (DoJ) against 15 Minneapolis protesters, accused of a "conspiracy" to "impede" US immigration officers. The operation followed a directive from Trump's executive order designating "antifa" a "domestic terrorist organization."

Major organizations allegedly connected to the "criminal conspiracy" included national labor unions like AFL-CIO and SEIU, local unions, and large left-leaning groups such as the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ). None of these organizations have been charged with any crimes.

DHS investigators obtained financial records of unions and non-profits under the guise of an inquiry into "domestic terrorist financing." This included using administrative subpoenas to get wire transfers from SEIU and requesting financial data from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York for the Communications Workers of America.

Undercover agents actively participated in activist events, with one report documenting "undercover agent activity" on January 31 at a Sunrise Movement "resistance skills training" at a public library. The agent described discussions on recruitment and "de-escalation," noting the organization focused on "peaceful" protests.

Civil rights groups have raised concerns that the federal government is criminalizing lawful protest activity by labeling it "leftwing terrorism." The scope and methods of the investigation have been criticized for an "apparent lack of investigative discipline."
